subject: Retention evidence & deletion runbook for HealthMax - timeline and on-demand retrieval
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@healthmax.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: security@healthmax.com
Date: 2027-05-23T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: retention evidence, temporary retain and on-demand retrieval

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this. As part of HealthMax's upcoming audit we need two things clarified for our DPA annex:

1) A short, timestamped listing of the backup purge timeline for our account (last 12 months).
2) The documented operational runbook for temporary-retain / emergency rollback (who executes, SLA for retrieval, steps to rehydrate logs).
3) Subprocessor list with data transfer locations for backups (we need to confirm no third-country transfers without SCCs).

Can you provide the above or point us to the evidence bundle? Our auditor has a hard cutoff in two weeks.

Attachments: SOC2-Audit-Requests.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Head of Privacy Operations
HealthMax
From: priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@healthmax.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention evidence, temporary retain and on-demand retrieval

Maria —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level responses below and a proposed runbook attached (proposed-runbook-v1.md). We can deliver a timestamped export for the last 12 months by next Tuesday EOD.

Quick summary:
- Backup purge timeline: automated daily snapshots; 30-day rolling hot retention, 180-day cold snapshot tier (per account), 540-day escrow for legal holds. I'll attach the exported audit CSV with purge timestamps once generated.
- Temporary-retain runbook: see attached. Key points:
  • Requester: HealthMax security or legal submits a signed retention request form.
  • Execution: infra ops (Karthik) triggers snapshot hold + copies to immutable escrow bucket.
  • Retrieval SLA: 24-72 hours depending on restore size; for logs under 50GB typical 6–12 hours.
  • Rollback steps: verification checklist -> restore to sandbox -> integrity check -> promote to production path.
- Subprocessors: we rely on CloudStore Inc. for long-term object storage and FastEdge for cross-region caching. Both entries include contract references (SCCs in place).

Next steps:
1) Karthik, please confirm the retrieval SLA numbers and add any escalation contacts.
2) Markus, can you confirm the escrow retention timeframe and whether we can provide notarized logs for audit?
3) Maria — will you accept a combined evidence bundle (CSV timestamps + runbook + subprocessor matrix) by Tue 25 May?

Attachment: proposed-runbook-v1.md (text)

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention evidence, temporary retain and on-demand retrieval

Looping in ops details and a few clarifications. Quoting Maria's ask below for context: 

> "A short, timestamped listing of the backup purge timeline for our account (last 12 months)."

Operational notes (short):
- We can produce: daily snapshot manifest with purge timestamps (CSV), S3 object delete logs for purge operations, and immutable escrow copy manifests.
- Retrieval SLA breakdown (typical):
  • Small restores (<50GB): 6–12 hours (target)
  • Medium restores (50–500GB): 12–36 hours
  • Large restores (>500GB): 24–72 hours (depends on transfer throughput)
- On-demand retrieval process:
  1) HealthMax sends signed temporary-retain form (DocuSign link accepted).
  2) Ops validates legal hold flags, snapshots are snapshotted to escrow bucket and ACL set to immutable.
  3) Retrieval ticket opened in Jira; assigned to infra on-call.
  4) Integrity checks + sha256 verification; provide logs back to HealthMax security.

Notes for Markus / Legal:
- If auditor requests notarized evidence we can provide time-signed manifests (cloud provider KMS sig) but notarization requires an extra legal step (we have vendor that does timestamp attestations, add 48–72 hours).
- Subprocessor exposures: CloudStore stores in us-east-1 and eu-west-1; transfers from eu to us are via SCCs (we have executed SCCs with CloudStore).

Attachments referenced: subprocessor-matrix-20270523.csv (csv)

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@healthmax.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: security@healthmax.com, vendor-security@cloudstorage.io
Date: 2027-05-24T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention evidence, temporary retain and on-demand retrieval

Thanks Priya and Karthik — that looks good and addresses most of the auditor's checklist. A few follow-ups before we close the ticket:

- Please include the exact timestamps (UTC) and a short note for any manual interventions over the last 12 months (e.g., emergency restores, legal holds).
- We would like a point-of-contact for on-demand retrieval (name + pager) for escalation during the audit window.
- Please provide the signed SCC copy for CloudStore (if available) and the KMS signing metadata referenced by Karthik.

If you can get the evidence bundle (CSV + runbook + subprocessor matrix + SCC copy + KMS metadata) to the DocuSign link / shared drive referenced, we'll mark the item resolved.

Best,
Maria Lopez
Head of Privacy Operations | HealthMax
